articles.body: India’s para-athletes will begin a packed day of competition at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on Monday, October 19, following the opening ceremony on Sunday. Several Indian stars, including Nishad Kumar, Avani Lekhara, Sheetal Devi, Harvinder Singh and Pramod Bhagat, will be in action across multiple disciplines.India will compete in para athletics, para badminton, para swimming, para archery, para shooting, para powerlifting, para table tennis, boccia, blind football and para cycling, with several medal events scheduled throughout the day.Nishad Kumar, Deepthi Jeevanji Lead Athletics ChallengeNishad Kumar will compete in the men’s long jump T47 final at 1:40 PM IST, while Deepthi Jeevanji is scheduled to participate in the women’s 400m T20 heats at 2:10 PM. Ajeet Singh Yadav and Rinku Hooda will feature in the men’s javelin throw F46 final at 3:35 PM, followed by Radha Venkatesh and Soumya in the women’s 1500m T12/T13 final at 3:55 PM. Pranav Desai will compete in the men’s 200m T64 final at 4:30 PM.Avani Lekhara, Sheetal Devi Among Key Names in ActionAvani Lekhara and Mona Agarwal will compete in the women’s R2 10m air rifle standing SH1 qualification at 6:30 AM IST. Bhagat will later partner Sukant Kadam in the men’s doubles SL3-SU5 match against Indonesia at noon.India’s Medal Events in Para Swimming and PowerliftingIndia will have several medal opportunities in para swimming. Gopichand Lingutla and Niranjan Mukundan are scheduled for the men’s 400m freestyle S7 final at 1:30 PM, followed by Vaishnavi Jagtap in the women’s 400m freestyle S8 final at 1:38 PM. Himanshu Nandal and Ravi Budigina will also compete in swimming finals during the afternoon.In para powerlifting, Jaspreet Kaur will contest the women’s 45kg final at 1:00 PM, while Manish Kumar and Paramjeet Kumar will compete in the men’s 59kg final at 2:30 PM.India Face Thailand in Blind FootballIndia’s men’s blind football team will take on Thailand in a preliminary-round match at 9:00 AM IST. articles.title: “My wages will go over to a local children's charity”: How David Beckham turned his PSG farewell into a charitable pledge
articles.summary: David Beckham has spent more than two decades supporting children through his work with UNICEF, from helping families affected by disasters to backing
articles.body: David Beckham has spent more than two decades supporting children through his work with UNICEF, from helping families affected by disasters to backing programmes against bullying, violence and child marriage. In 2013, the former England captain pledged his entire Paris Saint-Germain salary to a local children’s charity. Two years later, he launched 7: The David Beckham UNICEF Fund to support children facing serious risks. His work has taken him to countries including Sierra Leone, the Philippines and Indonesia, where he has used his fame to bring attention to children’s needs.How did David Beckham turn his football career into a long-term commitment to children’s welfare?David Beckham became a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador in 2005. By then, he had already made his name at Manchester United and was known far beyond football. His later career took him to Real Madrid, LA Galaxy, AC Milan and Paris Saint-Germain, but his work for children developed alongside his time on the pitch.Instead of limiting his support to public appearances, Beckham worked with the organisation on issues affecting children, including preventable disease, hunger, violence and access to education. His visits to communities gave him opportunities to meet children and families directly and show the challenges they faced.In 2008, Beckham travelled to Sierra Leone to draw attention to the country’s high infant mortality rate. The visit focused on child survival and the need for better healthcare. A year later, he travelled to South Africa to highlight efforts to prevent HIV from passing from mothers to their babies.These visits helped connect his public profile with specific issues affecting children. His role was not to replace medical teams or aid workers, but to help bring wider attention to their work and encourage support for programmes designed to protect young lives.Why did David Beckham donate his Paris Saint-Germain salary to charity in 2013?In January 2013, Beckham joined Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) on a five-month contract. He was 37 and approaching the end of his playing career, but his arrival in Paris also brought a major charitable pledge.At his unveiling, Beckham announced that he would not keep his wages from the French club. Instead, the money would go to a local children’s charity. The move meant that his final months as a professional player in France would also support children in need.Beckham explained his decision in simple terms: “It’s something I’m passionate about—children and charities,” Beckham remarked at the time. “We decided on something quite unique… my wages will go over to a local children’s charity. It’s one of the things I’m very excited and proud to be able to do”.The exact value of his full salary was not publicly confirmed when he made the announcement. The BBC reported on January 31, 2013, that the donation would be worth at least £1 million. Later reports linked part of the pledge to Necker Children’s Hospital in Paris and another charity, although the full distribution was not officially confirmed in the initial announcement.The decision stood out because Beckham was giving up his earnings from the contract rather than simply making a separate donation. It also gave the Paris move a purpose beyond football, with the money intended to help children and families in the French capital.What did David Beckham’s 7 Fund do for children across different countries?In February 2015, Beckham and UNICEF launched 7: The David Beckham UNICEF Fund. The launch marked his tenth year as a Goodwill Ambassador. Named after the shirt number closely linked to his career, the fund was created to support children facing violence, abuse, poor access to education and other serious risks.Its work covered several countries, with programmes shaped around local needs. In Indonesia, the fund supported efforts to prevent bullying and violence in schools. During a visit to Semarang in March 2018, Beckham met students involved in peer-led programmes that encouraged children to speak up about bullying and help make classrooms safer.One of the students he met was Sripun, a 15-year-old who had become a student leader in the effort to prevent school violence. The programme trained selected students to promote safer behaviour among their peers, while teachers learned ways to maintain classrooms free from violence.The work extended beyond Indonesia. In Uganda, programmes supported girls’ education and helped young people stay in school. In Nepal, funding helped support mental health and emotional support programmes for pupils. In El Salvador, the fund backed efforts to create safe places where children could learn and play, alongside stronger child-protection services.UNICEF reported in March 2018 that its wider work supported by the fund had included vaccinating 400,000 children against polio in Djibouti, helping 15,000 children access clean drinking water in Burkina Faso and protecting 14,500 children from violence and abuse in Cambodia. These figures refer to specific programmes and should not be treated as a single total of children reached by the fund.The central idea was to address problems that can stop children from learning, feeling safe or building a better future. Rather than focusing only on emergency donations, the fund supported work intended to help children over time.How did David Beckham support children affected by disasters in the Philippines and Ukraine?Beckham’s work with UNICEF has also focused on children caught up in emergencies. In November 2013, Typhoon Haiyan struck the Philippines, leaving communities devastated and forcing many families from their homes. Beckham helped raise awareness of the crisis and later visited survivors in the country in 2014, meeting children and families affected by the disaster.His visits helped bring attention to the need for emergency supplies and longer-term support for children dealing with the effects of losing their homes, relatives and access to school.In March 2022, after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Beckham and his wife, Victoria Beckham, supported a UNICEF emergency appeal for children and families affected by the war. The appeal focused on urgent needs, including medical supplies and safe spaces for families.Beckham also gave Dr. Iryna Kondratova, who headed a regional perinatal centre in Kharkiv, access to his Instagram account. She used the platform to show the conditions faced by medical staff caring for mothers and newborn babies during the conflict. The account takeover helped bring international attention to the challenges of providing care while attacks threatened hospitals and homes.The effort showed how Beckham could use his large social media audience to share information from people working on the ground. Rather than speaking for the medical staff, he gave them a platform to explain their work and the risks facing families.UNICEF’s records confirm his involvement in the Ukraine appeal and the Instagram takeover. articles.title: “My family and I are horrified seeing pictures”: How Roger Federer and Mirka’s $100M+ educational mission reached over 3.8 million children
articles.summary: Roger Federer and his wife, Mirka Federer, have helped bring educational opportunities to more than 3.82 million children through their foundation, which
articles.body: Roger Federer and his wife, Mirka Federer, have helped bring educational opportunities to more than 3.82 million children through their foundation, which was established in 2003. By the end of 2025, the organisation had also strengthened 18,445 educational institutions and supported training for more than 72,000 teachers. Its work focuses on early childhood education in Southern Africa and Switzerland, helping children develop basic learning skills before entering primary school. In April 2026, the organisation adopted the name Federer Foundation as it began a new five-year strategy.How did Roger Federer and Mirka Federer begin their educational mission?Roger Federer established the foundation on December 24, 2003, shortly after winning his first Wimbledon singles title that summer. At just 22, he was building a career that would eventually bring him 20 Grand Slam singles titles. However, his plans for helping children began long before he became one of tennis’s biggest names.Federer’s connection to Southern Africa came partly through his mother, Lynette Federer, who grew up in South Africa. His visits to the region helped him understand the difficulties faced by children who lacked access to quality education. Rather than waiting until his playing career ended, he decided to support children while continuing to compete.His wife, Mirka Federer, a former professional tennis player, also became involved in the foundation’s development. She is now a member of its board of trustees, alongside Roger and his mother. The organisation’s early work included helping individual children with school fees, meals, uniforms and sports coaching. Over time, its focus shifted towards improving early education systems and helping entire communities.The foundation now works across Southern Africa and Switzerland. Its main focus is to give young children the chance to learn, play and develop skills that will help them as they move through school.According to the Federer Foundation, its work is built around cooperation with governments, local organisations and communities rather than running a separate education system of its own.Why does Roger Federer’s foundation focus on early childhood education?The foundation concentrates on children in their early years, particularly those between the ages of three and eight. This is when children begin to develop language, social skills, confidence and the ability to learn. If they miss out on these early experiences, they may find it harder to keep up when they start primary school.Its work covers South Africa, Namibia, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Malawi and Lesotho, alongside education and inclusion projects in Switzerland. By the end of 2025, the foundation had reached 3.82 million children and strengthened 18,445 educational institutions. It had also supported the training of more than 72,000 teachers. These figures show how its work has grown from helping individual students to supporting education across entire communities.One of its major programmes is the School Readiness Initiative, which helps preschools prepare children for primary school. In South Africa, the programme works with community-based early learning centres, including small preschools that may not have the same resources as larger institutions.The aim is to improve the quality of teaching and make sure children have the support they need before entering Grade 1. Teachers receive guidance on how young children learn, while local partners work to improve learning spaces and classroom activities.Food is another part of the effort. Children who arrive at school hungry can struggle to focus, so feeding programmes and community gardens help address a problem that can affect both attendance and learning. The idea is to make it easier for children to attend preschool regularly and take part in classroom activities.The foundation also works with local organisations and public authorities to help keep these programmes running over time. Communities have a role in the process, helping build local ownership instead of relying entirely on outside support. This approach is intended to make improvements last beyond the period covered by a particular grant.How did Roger Federer’s Match in Africa raise millions for children?Federer has also used his popularity as a tennis star to raise money for children’s education. His Match in Africa exhibition series brought together well-known names from sport and entertainment, with the proceeds supporting the foundation’s work.The biggest edition took place on February 7, 2020, at Cape Town Stadium in South Africa. Federer faced his longtime rival Rafael Nadal in an exhibition match, while philanthropist Bill Gates and comedian Trevor Noah took part in the doubles match before it.The event drew 51,954 spectators, setting a world record for attendance at a tennis match at the time. It also raised $3.5 million for the foundation, with the net proceeds directed towards educational programmes in the region. The event gave fans an opportunity to watch two leading players compete while helping raise money for children who needed better access to early learning.The exhibition was more than a tennis match. It brought attention to the education challenges facing children in the region and showed how a major sporting event could help fund work outside the court.Federer’s connection to the cause also extended beyond the stadium. His foundation’s programmes focus on children in local communities, where access to preschool education and trained teachers can make a real difference. The money raised through the event helped support that wider effort.The Match in Africa became an important example of how Federer combined his sporting career with charitable work. Instead of keeping his public profile separate from the foundation, he used it to bring supporters and funding to a cause he had backed since his early years as a professional player.How did Roger Federer support Ukrainian children during the war?The foundation’s work has also extended beyond its long-term education programmes in Africa. In March 2022, after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Federer announced a $500,000 donation to help children affected by the war continue their education.The money was pledged through War Child Holland, an organisation that supports children affected by conflict. The donation was intended to help Ukrainian children access continued schooling during a period when many had been forced to leave their homes.Federer explained his concern in a message about the situation, saying:“My family and I are horrified seeing pictures from Ukraine and heartbroken for the innocent people who have been so terribly affected,” Federer wrote. “About six million Ukrainian children are currently out of school… we would like to support them.”The donation reflected the foundation’s wider aim of helping children continue learning when circumstances make education difficult. While its main programmes focus on Southern Africa and Switzerland, the support for Ukrainian children showed that Federer was also prepared to help during an international crisis.The $500,000 pledge was a separate response to the war, rather than part of the foundation’s regular early learning programmes. Its purpose was to help children whose education had been disrupted by the conflict.For Federer, the issue was not limited to getting children into classrooms. It was also about helping them continue learning during a frightening and uncertain period in their lives.The foundation’s broader work continues to focus on building stronger early education systems. In April 2026, it introduced a new strategy for 2026 to 2030 and adopted the name Federer Foundation. articles.title: From selling vegetables to Commonwealth medal: Now Jhandu Kumar dreams of Paralympic glory
articles.summary: Kolkata: Not too long ago, Jhandu Kumar used to sell vegetables and drive an e-rickshaw to meet his own expenses and help run the family household.
articles.body: Kolkata: Not too long ago, Jhandu Kumar used to sell vegetables and drive an e-rickshaw to meet his own expenses and help run the family household. Today, the Bihar para-powerlifter is a Commonwealth Games bronze medallist, has secured a government job and is preparing to represent India at Asian Para Games.For Jhandu, who finished on the podium in the men’s heavyweight para-powerlifting event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games with a 190kg lift, the transformation still feels like a dream.“Yes, absolutely. It feels like a dream. A boy from a village who worked hard is now making a name for himself across the country,” Jhandu told TOI from Aichi-Nagoya. “I cannot express how happy I am. Words fail me. Now I have another opportunity at the Asian Para Games to represent my country.”The athlete from Harnaut village in Bihar’s Nalanda district will compete in the 72kg category on Tuesday. He continued his training for the Games at the National Centre of Excellence in Gandhinagar under coach Rajinder Singh Rahelu. More than making drastic changes to his training, he concentrated on strengthening the self-belief that has driven his rise.“The basic approach remains the same. For me, it is about maintaining that inner drive and staying motivated. I have this determination within me: ‘I will do it, I will definitely succeed,’” said the 29-year-old. “That has been my main focus, to perform even better.”However, Jhandu knows there will be little margin for error in a competitive field. Asked what sort of lift could put him in medal contention, he said the numbers alone would not determine the outcome.“A medal could come at 200kg, 205kg or even 190kg. During competition, the mind works differently. You have to manage everything, and there is pressure,” he said. “You have to handle that pressure, and then it depends on how your body responds and how much you can push yourself.”Irrespective of the numbers, Jhandu expects stiff competition and is relishing the challenge. “There are many strong competitors. Lifter from China and Malaysia will be among them, apart from athletes from several other countries. Competition is inevitable. In fact, without competition, it would not be exciting,” Jhandu said.Despite all that he has achieved, Jhandu admits his journey still feels surreal. “Honestly, I never imagined that I would one day compete at Commonwealth Games or Asian Para Games. My focus was simply on working hard and winning a medal for my country,” he said.That hard work has paid off, and the medal in Glasgow did more than establish Jhandu on the international stage. It changed his life back home, too. The reception he received and the support from the Bihar govt, including a govt job, have given him even greater motivation to succeed.None of it, he believes, would have been possible without his family’s support.“My family has always been a huge source of motivation and support. They supported me even when I was selling vegetables and driving an e-rickshaw,” said the para-lifter, who was affected by polio at the age of five. “It is difficult to put into words how much my family has done for me.”The Asian Para Games may be the immediate assignment, but Jhandu already has a bigger destination in mind. “My main target is the Paralympics. I am determined to win a Paralympic medal for India,” he said. “I am prepared to put in whatever hard work is required.”For the boy from a small village in Bihar, the journey that once seemed unimaginable has only made him dream bigger.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Carolina Hurricanes Continue To Be Handed Tough News As Mark Jankowski Sent Back To Raleigh For Evaluation
articles.summary: Already depleted by significant losses to the forward group, Carolina’s center depth faces a critical test as Mark Jankowski joins the growing injury list.
articles.body:
The Carolina Hurricanes continue to be burdened with a growing injury list, as yet another of the team's forwards has been sidelined.

Centerman Mark Jankowski was ruled out before Sunday's game against the Calgary Flames with a lower-body injury, with Carolina coach Rod Brind'Amour saying postgame that he had been sent back to Raleigh for further evaluation.

"I don't even know what happened, but we sent him home to get looked at," Brind'Amour said. "I don't have any other update than that."

The loss of Jankowski, who was on a six-game goal streak before the injury, is a rather large one too considering that he was already playing higher up in the lineup due to the injuries the team was already dealing with.

Jordan Staal is out for the next one to two months due to a partial calf tear and so Jankowski was taking on a lot of the captain's responsibilities.

So without both, the team's center depth has taken a huge blow, especially when it comes to the defensive side of the game.

The loss of Jankowski is the fourth forward to be sidelined this year, joining Staal, Taylor Hall and Seth Jarvis.

The Hurricanes already had a pair of rookies filling in in Bradly Nadeau and Felix Unger Sorum, but now the Jankowski loss may prompt another move given the Canes only have three centers on the roster.

"Obviously there's been a lot of guys getting nicked up here to start the year," said alternate captain Jordan Martinook who filled in at center on Sunday. "I think forever around here it's been the next-man-up mentality. That's not going to change anytime soon. I think everyone is comfortable with whoever we put in. It's just the way it is right now."

articles.title: "Hay que visibilizar que el deporte es un tratamiento más en los procesos oncológicos"
articles.standfirst: El Reto Pelayo Vida, en su undécima edición, vuelve a África • Serán 16 días de ciclismo y kayak • El objetivo, sensibilizar sobre el cáncer en las mujeres
articles.summary: El Reto Pelayo Vida, en su undécima edición, vuelve a África • Serán 16 días de ciclismo y kayak • El objetivo, sensibilizar sobre el cáncer en las mujeres
articles.body: Pelear contra un cáncer no es algo que uno elija, es una vivencia impuesta que implica miedos y demanda valor. No es un proceso bonito, pero superar la enfermedad es un gran motivo de celebración. Es aquí donde entra el Reto Pelayo Vida, el mayor proyecto deportivo de sensibilización sobre el cáncer de la mujer, que va a por su duodécima edición. En este caso se trata de un desafío elegido que pretende celebrar la vida a través del deporte, esa herramienta tan necesaria para nuestra salud física y mental. Este año el Reto Pelayo Vida regresa a sus orígenes, a África, el continente donde hace 11 años tuvo lugar un ascenso al Kilimanjaro inolvidable que demostró que los sueños son posibles tras la enfermedad. Esta edición se ha seleccionado a cinco expedicionarias -de entre 533 candidatas- a las que les espera un recorrido en bicicleta y kayak por Senegal que ha creado el director deportivo del proyecto Antonio de la Rosa. El reto se extenderá durante 16 días (24 noviembre a 9 de diciembre) y arrancará en la costa cercana a Dakar; avanzará hacia el sur del país, atravesando reservas naturales, sabanas y el espectacular Delta del Sine-Saloum hasta llegar a la región de Casamance. Un reto que exigirá resistencia física, adaptación constante y un fuerte espíritu de equipo. Las protagonistas serán Irantzu Pinillos (Pamplona), Marta García Bodí (Valencia), Vanesa Amigo (Madrid/A Coruña), Milena Amelibia (San Sebastián) y Noemí Carrasco (Madrid/Sevilla). Su objetivo final, ser un ejemplo de superación para otras mujeres y llevar su mensaje a millones de personas recordando que el deporte puede ser una poderosa herramienta de recuperación, motivación y vida. “Suena muy bonito y muy especial esta aventura, hacemos bromas sobre lo que nos vamos a encontrar, pero para superar el reto todas nos hemos preparado mucho durante los últimos meses”, recalcan ellas. Están ilusionadas y aventurarse en lo desconocido da la impresión de ser un chute de vitalidad. La pamplonesa Irantzu Pinillos, de 47 años, residente en Estella-Lizarra (Navarra), ha padecido cáncer de mama. “Una amiga madrileña me habló del Reto Pelayo y me vi los documentales. Me visualicé haciéndolo, aunque te apuntas a ciegas, sin saber dónde tendrá lugar el reto”, señala. “Me hicieron una mastectomía y tuve que estar bastantes semanas sin hacer deporte y yo antes de la operación hacía bici de montaña. Estaba esperando que el médico me diera el visto bueno para salir y en cuanto me dio permiso fui a la montaña con la bicicleta. Eso me ayudó mucho a recuperar la confianza en mi cuerpo, porque no sabía cómo iba a cicatrizar la herida y si iba a tener secuelas. Verme encima de la bici pedaleando con fuerza y energía era una motivación, era bueno para mi confianza y autoestima, era algo que necesitaba para mi bienestar emocional, fue un revulsivo maravilloso”. Marta García Bodí, de 42 años, es de Valencia y en 2023 recibió el diagnóstico de cáncer de ovario mientras estaba embarazada. Como ella dice, “mi hijo me salvó la vida”. Marta explica: “Pertenezco a la ‘Asociación A Saco’ y me informaron del reto. Yo estaba en un momento bajo cuando lo conocí, pero ya le dije a mi familia que al año siguiente me apuntaba y aquí estoy”. El deporte tuvo que esperar un poco: “En mi caso me operaron y me trataron con quimioterapia estando embarazada. Físicamente me costó y mi padre me llevó un par de veces a una clínica de fisioterapia para moverme más. Soy muy enérgica y positiva, pero el cuerpo no me daba. Tras nacer mi hijo tuve algunas secuelas en la pierna derecha y comencé a hacer un trabajo de fuerza para mover esa pierna y a día de hoy el deporte es fundamental y es la medicina que yo misma me puedo aplicar”. “Arrullaba a mi hijo Nico haciendo sentadillas”, bromea Marta. Vanesa Amigo, de 45 años, es originaria de Alcorcón (Madrid) pero gallega de adopción, pues reside en A Coruña desde hace 15 años. Madre de dos hijos -9 y 11 años-, fue campeona de España de gimnasia rítmica (en conjunto y en individual). En 2024 le diagnosticaron cáncer de mama. “Mi cuñado fue quien me contó de la existencia del reto, curioseé en la página y me apunté, pero en ningún momento pensé que iba a estar hoy aquí”, nos cuenta Vanesa. No duda en su mensaje y consejo al mismo tiempo: “El deporte para mí va en vena. Competí desde los 5 a los 20 años y eso me dio una disciplina y autocontrol que ha marcado mi personalidad. Los dos primeros meses después de la operación fueron duros porque no tenía el permiso del cirujano para poder moverme y eso me bloqueó. Cuando ya tuve el permiso, el deporte fue una terapia, fue mi tratamiento principal más que la pastilla que me tenía que tomar todos los días o más que cualquier otra cosa. Fue mi vía de escape, la manara de volver a sentirme yo, de volver a reencontrarme conmigo misma. El deporte puede dar pereza, pero yo siempre pienso en lo bien que me siento después”. Milena Amelibia, de 42 años, es de San Sebastián, donde trabaja como matrona. En 2019, cuando tenía 35 años, fue diagnosticada de un cáncer de ovario. Así se embarcó en esta aventura: “Fue en una asociación donde me enteré del Reto Pelayo Vida. Me encanta caminar por la montaña en invierno y vi que el año pasado el reto fue en Patagonia. Veía a aquellas mujeres acampar sobre el hielo y me pareció muy inspirador. Pensé, ‘¿por qué no puedo ser yo? Yo habría tirado hacia el frío, pero nos vamos a Senegal y creo que me va a encantar”. Milena también sacó provecho de su afición deportiva: “Durante el tratamiento no era capaz de hacer deporte, pero me ponía retos físicos. Mi refugio fue escaparme a la montaña los días que estaba mejor. Yo me he apoyado en el deporte sobre todo a posteriori, para reconstruirme; la montaña, a nivel físico y mental, ha sido un antidepresivo. Tener mis objetivos me ha ayudado mucho a retomar una vida activa y saludable. Esas ilusiones y proyectos que a veces se apagan por culpa de la enfermedad, el deporte los reactiva”. Noemí Carrasco, de 42 años, nació en Madrid pero reside desde hace 13 años en Sevilla. Sufrió cáncer de tiroides con ocho años y cáncer de mama llamado Phylloides, que es poco común, recientemente. “¿Cómo he llegado aquí? Una amiga me veía en este reto. Esa mezcla de deporte, aventura, demostrarme a mí misma que he superado esta enfermedad y que estoy más fuerte que nunca, y la oportunidad de enviar un mensaje de esperanza a mujeres que lo están pasando mal, es lo que me motivaba para formar parte de este reto”, narra Noemí. La madrileña destaca sobre la importancia del deporte: “A mí el deporte me ha permitido pasar mejor el cáncer. Gracias a Dios se empieza a hablar del deporte como una parte importante en la recuperación del cáncer, pero creo que hay que visibilizarlo como un tratamiento más en los procesos oncológicos. Es necesario para mantener tu masa muscular y estar fuerte durante los tratamientos. Es un antidepresivo y permite que tu mente esté puesta en algo positivo”.

articles.body:
Kyren Williams was not happy with his season-low 13 touches to the ball after the Los Angeles Rams' 18-16 upset loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon.

Williams has been playing in the NFL since 2022, going through his fifth season with the Rams. He embraced the starting job in 2023 and never looked back, enjoying great campaigns in the potent attack featuring Matthew Stafford and Puka Nacua.

However, he didn't have the high activity in Los Angeles' game against Arizona. He only racked up 10 carries for 50 yards while catching three passes for 17 yards. The star rusher reflected on his performance after the game, expressing frustration about the lack of usage, per reporter Sarah Barshop.

"Kyren Williams was asked why he thought the team couldn't sustain the energy drive to drive," Barshop wrote.

"Can't tell you, bro. Probably because I'm not out there," Williams said.

How Kyren Williams, Rams played against Cardinals

Kyren Williams knows he is more than capable of performing at a high level. He just needs the Rams to count on him for that, which they didn't do in their loss to the Cardinals.

Los Angeles massively underperformed on the offensive side of the ball. Against an Arizona squad where they were the heavy favorites, the hosts couldn't create more touchdown drives or take advantage of errors that the Cardinals would make.

Matthew Stafford was active with his passing, but he didn't give the usual high attention to his star receivers. He completed 25 out of 33 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns.

Blake Corum was a bright spot in the offense, having nine carries for 42 yards while catching two passes for 18 yards and a touchdown. Puka Nacua led receivers with six catches for 80 yards, while Davante Adams caught three passes for 39 yards. Meanwhile, Colby Parkinson had five receptions for 31 yards and a touchdown.

articles.title: Tiki Barber Reveals What’s Wrong With Giants’ Cam Skattebo
articles.summary: The New York Giants made the interesting choice on Sunday to “downgrade” their usual starting running back, Cam Skattebo. Their 2025 fourth-round draft pick,...
articles.body:
The New York Giants made the interesting choice on Sunday to "downgrade" their usual starting running back, Cam Skattebo.

Their 2025 fourth-round draft pick, after a fumble in Week 5 against the Washington Commanders, was essentially banished to the shadow realm. He didn't receive any rushing attempts or any targets in the passing game either.

This is a guy who has eight total touchdowns in 13 career games, by the way, and has typically been a consistent producer when healthy.

So what's the deal with Skattebo? Was his benching really due to just the ill-timed fumble in Washington? Or is there something deeper going on between the second-year running back and the Giants coaching staff?

Tiki Barber Says 'Negative Plays' Hurting Cam Skattebo

On WFAN's New York Giants postgame coverage, legendary running back and current radio analyst Tiki Barber revealed some damning details regarding the 24-year-old Skattebo.

"There have been a lot of negative plays for him. And it's misreading the run game, or being too fast in the run game…so many other things that matter to be on the field for 3rd Down…knowing protection responsibility," Barber said, via WFAN's Kris Pursiainen.

"Those little things that are considered 'busts' aren't as obvious to the lay fan, but I think there's been a lot of those for Cam Skattebo for this season…he presented it as the fumble…I think it was more than that. In fact, I know it was more than that."

Barber clearly has a little inside information here. As a Giants franchise legend, he has some connections with the organization, and someone may have let something slip to the current analyst.

Regardless, Barber knows what he's looking at. With a 10-year career under his belt, the former All-Pro knows the running back position as well as anyone on the planet.

Barber also refers to Skattebo's post-game answer as to why he was benched. He told reporters, "I got punished for what I did. I understand it, so I gotta be ready when coach calls my name, and that wasn't today," via The Athletic's Charlotte Carroll.

But maybe Skattebo also knows a little more than what he's letting on.

It's tough to say how much the absence of Skattebo impacted the New York Giants' run game against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, but it's safe to say, as a whole, it wasn't good.

In his absence, the trio of Tyrone Tracy, Najee Harris, and Devin Singletary received 14 carries, turning it into 36 total rushing yards. All in all, a pretty putrid outing from New York's running backs.

Harbaugh is clearly looking for someone to establish themselves as the Giants' bell-cow running back, and he said as much after the game .

"One of those guys needs to step up. Somebody needs to step up and be the back. None of those guys have done that yet. When one of those guys steps up to be the back, then they'll be the back."

We'll see if Skattebo is able to re-establish himself in Week 7 after some time in the doghouse.

articles.title: Bills HC Joe Brady in awe of rookie’s ‘stickiness’ in win vs. Raiders
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills returned to the winning column after suffering their first loss of the season, handing the Las Vegas Raiders a 33-30 loss in Week 6 of the...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills returned to the winning column after suffering their first loss of the season, handing the Las Vegas Raiders a 33-30 loss in Week 6 of the NFL season. While the spotlight largely remained on Josh Allen and James Cook for their heroic performances, Bills head coach Joe Brady made sure to highlight rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun's 'stickiness' in coverage following the win.

During his postgame press conference, Brady praised Igbinosun's ability to remain close to opposing receivers and continue competing regardless of the outcome of individual plays.

"We were a little matchier today in coverage, and the stickiness kind of showed, and that's what IGB kind of does," Brady said. "And what I love about IGB is he just keeps playing, and they might take a shot, and he's going to go right back at it with the same mindset."

"He has a short memory, and so he's continuing to grow game in game out and us getting a feel for what's best for him, but one thing I know is he competes every damn play, and that's exactly what we're looking for."

Igbinosun delivered a notable performance against the Raiders, recording three pass deflections and two total tackles in Buffalo's narrow victory. The second-round pick out of Ohio State registered one solo tackle and one assisted tackle while helping the Bills disrupt Las Vegas' passing attack.

The rookie's performance provided an encouraging sign for Buffalo's secondary as the team looks to maintain its strong start to the season. The victory improved Buffalo's record to 5-1 this season.

However, the game was not without controversy for the Bills. Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the first half .

The win gives Brady's team additional momentum heading into its bye week. The Bills will have an opportunity to rest and address areas for improvement before hosting the Baltimore Ravens.

articles.title: 5 takeaways from Packers' 23-13 win vs Cowboys: Defense makes a statement
articles.summary: Jonathan Gannon's defense made a statement as Green Bay put the clamps on the Dallas defense in an important victory at Lambeau Field.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers defeated the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field by a 23-13 final score to claim their third straight win, taking them to 4-2 on the season.

Here are five takeaways from a big victory on "Sunday Night Football":

It is hard to overstate the job Jonathan Gannon and the Packers defense did in this matchup. In a game that was supposed to be a shootout, Gannon perplexed Dak Prescott all night, channeling his inner Brian Flores and leaving the Dallas quarterback unsure what was coming next.

This was not just smoke and mirrors though, the Packers' defensive players showed their quality, as they harassed the quarterback and even more impressively, the defensive backs held their own against CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, and then some.

This game was always going to serve as a test of just how good Green Bay's defense really is, and specifically whether it is good enough to compete in the postseason. The answer looks like a resounding yes.

While it was far from a flawless offensive performance, Jordan Love was in full command at the line of scrimmage on Sunday night, and Matt LaFleur kept pressing the right buttons with his play-calling.

The offensive line remains an issue and regressed somewhat from their recent performances. It is probably time for Kevin Zeitler to get into the lineup next week in Detroit. Mostly due to the offensive line, the run game was once again nonexistent.

But Love made none of that matter, as he simply kept making plays, and his stat line should have looked a lot more impressive.

The main reason Love's numbers are not as gaudy is because of some big drops. Matthew Golden dropped two touchdowns – although they did end up scoring on one of those drives anyway – and Christian Watson dropped one as well.

Ultimately, it did not hurt them tonight, and that has mostly been the case this season, as the Packers offense is often explosive enough to overcome their mistakes. It is an issue that needs cleaning up though.

After a concerning performance at Lambeau Field a week ago, and with the wind whipping again, it was an important night for Trey Smack, and he rebounded, nailing every kick.

He is likely to go through ups and downs throughout his rookie year, but it seems the Packers did not lose confidence in him, and he rewarded their faith on Sunday night. Hopefully he can build on this performance moving forward.

Not for the first time this season, the officials threatened to spoil a strong Packers performance on defense. Craig Wrolstad and his crew extended a Cowboys drive multiple times by throwing flags for extremely soft roughing the passer offences and other nebulous issues.

They robbed Carrington Valentine of what would have been an awesome moment as he picked off Prescott because Lukas Van Ness lightly pushed the Cowboys quarterback in a way that happens around 20 times in an average NFL game.

The officiating in the league has become egregiously bad.

Instead of accounting for the fact they seem to not know what they are looking at by getting out of the way unless something is an obvious penalty, especially on third and fourth down, they are inserting themselves into the action at every opportunity and at times changing the outcome of games.

It is an epidemic which must be stopped. The refs almost took the entire shine off the feeling of victory for the Packers tonight.

articles.title: Kirk Herbstreit Breaks Silence on Controversial Notre Dame-BYU Ending

articles.body:
The No. 2 Notre Dame Fighting Irish lost in dramatic fashion to the No. 8 BYU Cougars on Saturday night.

Notre Dame trailed 28-24 and had the ball at first-and-goal with just four seconds remaining on the clock.

Star quarterback CJ Carr threw an incomplete pass on a play that appeared to involve pass interference. However, officials called the game over without checking whether any time remained on the clock.

Just hours after the game, the Big 12 released a statement acknowledging that officials should have put one second back on the clock after Carr's incomplete pass. That would have given Notre Dame another opportunity to reach the end zone on second-and-goal.

"It was determined that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground and the play was incorrectly cleared by the replay officiating crew," the Big 12's statement read . "The Conference will conduct a complete review of its end-of-game officiating process in advance of next week's games."

Kirk Herbstreit Speaks on Notre Dame-BYU Game

Kirk Herbstreit, who called the game alongside Chris Fowler for ESPN on ABC, shared his thoughts on the finish and BYU's impressive performance on social media Sunday afternoon.

"Another week, another wild finish! A lot of talk about the ending, but let's not lose sight of what BYU did to put themselves in position to win this ballgame," Herbstreit said. "Tremendous effort by the Cougars to find a way to get it done. And of course don't count Notre Dame out… Still a lot of football left to be played!"

Herbstreit's takes on Notre Dame haven't been well received by the fanbase, especially after he recently criticized the team's schedule. However, he picked the Fighting Irish as his preseason national champion and has stood by that prediction.

articles.title: 3 things we learned about the Cowboys versus Packers
articles.summary: The losing streak continues
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys slipped to 2-4 on the season, as they look less and less like the team most envisioned coming into the season. After their loss to the Green Bay Packers, we learned some things.

Nothing has come easy for this team in the last two weeks. There is little-to-no room for error, and the Cowboys simply cannot stop making mistakes. Whether it's dropped balls, missed blocks, or just plain slipping – Dallas cannot get out their own way.

In the first half, the defense performed extremely well on first and second down. They could not get off the field on third, however, regardless of the distance. It didn't matter if the defense sent the heat on a blitz or if they dropped their guys back in coverage – the Packers and Jordan Love had their number.

In a way that wasn't supposed to happen this season, the offense mirrored the defense's inadequacies throughout the first half. Zero points scored paired with two turnovers on the plus side of the field is not the ideal situation.

Put it all together and you end the first half down by 17 points.

The defense did clamp down after half time, allowing just six points after the break. The offense never truly found their way, scoring just two touchdowns on the night.

Zero points in the first half, with 13 points on the board at the final whistle is not good enough, and will never be good enough with the way this Cowboys team is constructed. The team will win zero games if that's the offensive result each week.

This is a unit featuring some of the best playmakers in the NFL, yet for the second week in a row, they cannot adjust to the blitzing onslaught from their opponent. Dak Prescott was under assault the entire game, taking hit after hit, sometimes even resulting in personal fouls.

Everything is out of rhythm and very little is working. They need to figure out how to beat the blitz if they're going to have a chance on offense. This is a blueprint other teams will attempt to duplicate until Dallas can figure out how to stop it.

This team still refuses to run the ball, even when it's working. Balance does not seem to be something that Brian Schottenheimer is too interested in through six weeks, and especially the last two. Regardless of what the head coach says to the media, sticking with the run is clearly not in the forefront of the mind of the head coach and play caller.

Ten carries on the night for Javonte Williams until nearly two minutes left in the fourth quarter is inexcusable considering the game was well within reach for the entire second half. Dallas ran the ball five-out-of-nine plays on their opening drive of the second half, resulting in a touchdown. After that, there was not another run play called until nearly two minutes left in the fourth quarter.

The play-caller felt the pressure to put up points. It's possible he didn't trust his defense to get stops in the second half, which is reasonable. But the rushing attack was working, and it was completely abandoned when it wasn't necessary to do so. This offense needs balance if it's going to survive. Dak Prescott cannot throw the ball 50 plus times each week, or this could be the result.

articles.body: India’s Sheetal Devi delivered a record-breaking performance in the women’s compound archery qualification round at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya on Monday, scoring 704 out of a possible 720 points to equal the world record and establish a new Asian record.The 19-year-old archer from Jammu and Kashmir produced an exceptional display of accuracy, hitting 57 perfect 10s across her 72 arrows, including 32 Xs, which mark shots landing in the target’s innermost scoring zone.Her score surpassed the previous Asian record of 698 by six points, setting a new benchmark in the continental competition. The world record of 704 was established by Turkiye’s Oznur Girdi at the 2024 Paris Paralympic Games.Sheetal, a Paris Paralympics bronze medallist and reigning Asian Games champion, also eclipsed her own Asian Para Games record of 680, which she had set at Hangzhou in 2023. At that edition, she won two gold medals in the individual and mixed team events, along with a silver in doubles.She had raised the Asian record to 698 in March this year before taking it a step further with Monday’s record-equalling effort in Nagoya.Payal makes impressive Asian Games debutIndia also received a strong performance from debutant Payal, who scored 675 points in the women’s compound qualification round to finish fifth and bolster the country’s medal prospects in the individual and team competitions.The quadruple amputee from Odisha had attracted attention in April after defeating Sheetal on her way to winning gold at the World Archery Para Series in Bangkok.Their performances combined to give India the top spot in the women’s compound team qualification standings. Sheetal and Payal accumulated 1,379 points, finishing comfortably ahead of China, who managed 1,338.India’s position at the top secured the pair a direct entry into the semifinals. They will take on the winners of the quarterfinal between fifth-seeded Thailand and fourth-seeded Kazakhstan, with victory taking them into the medal round.Sheetal’s historic qualification score and Payal’s encouraging debut have given India a strong platform as the archery competition moves into the knockout stages.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Falcons HC Kevin Stefanski Gets Honest After Frustrating Loss to Bears
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons suffered their second straight loss by losing to the Chicago Bears 31-23.Bears quarterback Caleb Williams made his return after a three-g...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons suffered their second straight loss by losing to the Chicago Bears 31-23.

Bears quarterback Caleb Williams made his return after a three-game absence due to a hamstring. Williams showed no signs of rust by throwing for 305 yards and a touchdown against an impressive Falcons defense.

The Falcons came in being the number one rushing defense in the league and the team did a decent job of stopping the run for the most part.

"Williams was 12 of 12 for 142 yards before throwing his first incompletion in the second quarter," an ESPN article says. "Though the Bears won two of three games with Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum filing in at quarterback, Williams' return sparked the offense. He completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards with one touchdown."

Kevin Stefanski made it a focal point to start out fast against this Bears team.

"Instead, the visiting team raced out to a 14-0 lead in Mercedes-Benz Stadium," Will McFadden wrote in an Atlanta Falcons article . "The Bears built that lead up to 31-7 on the first play of the fourth quarter, a cushion large enough to withstand a furious Falcons rally that nearly turned the game on its head in the final 10 minutes. Tight end Kyle Pitts caught two touchdown passes in the fourth quarter to close the gap, but Atlanta ran out of time and couldn't overcome its slow start, losing 31-23."

Though Stefanski made it a focal point to start fast, as expected, he was not pleased with how the team started. It's one thing to talk about it, it's another thing to actually put it out on the field.

"I'm obviously proud of how we continue to fight, but to start like we started is really, really disappointing," head coach Kevin Stefanski said after the game . "That's something we talked at length about, and we talked at length about starting fast in this ballgame, and we did not."

"We've got to get that fixed because we just put ourselves in the hole," Stefanski said. "Disappointed. I'll have to look at how we start and make sure that we are putting our guys in position, but we will own that one, and we will move on."

Atlanta Could Not Get The Run Game Going

The identity of this Falcons team is to get Bijan Robinson and this run game going. Robinson was held to 61 yards on the ground, yet only carried the ball nine times.

"That's what we set our identity in: this run game," Robinson said after the game . "The run game gets everything going on this offense. So, for us, I know when we got down those scores, we were trying to play catch-up with the passes, so we could try to get as many yards as we can. When we run the ball effectively and have opportunities to run the ball, that's what makes our offense super hard to stop."

Well, the first mistake is that you didn't give your star running back the ball a few more times. Things go bad when you are one-dimensional.

Atlanta will have a chance to redeem themselves as they attempt to end their losing streak next week against the undefeated San Francisco 49ers .

articles.title: Thunder’s Jaylin Williams makes wild request after Cason Wallace’s contract extension

articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder opened up the brink trunks a few days before their season opener, agreeing to a contract extension with Cason Wallace worth five years and $139 million. It was the next highly anticipated extension for the franchise, especially given how Wallace has played over the past few years.

Moments after the extension was announced, Wallace went on Instagram and made a post, and his teammates were quick to comment. Jaylin Williams was one of the first, and he had a wild request after Wallace got paid.

"So you finna buy me you & K matching lambos," Williams wrote.

It was a bold request from Williams, and there's a good chance that since he's not a family member, he won't be getting any cars. If anything, Wallace is going to buy himself a car with the new money he has.

It's a well-deserved extension for Wallace, who is slated to be in the starting lineup this season after Lu Dort was traded to the Atlanta Hawks during the offseason. After his play last season and in the postseason, there were many people who expected that Wallace would see an increase in minutes this season, and even a larger role.

Wallace is one of the better defenders on the team, as well as an average 3-point shooter. He'll be playing more of the role that Dort had in the starting lineup, but Wallace has more shot creation in his game.

Though the Thunder lost key pieces during the offseason like Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe, they have enough depth on the team to fill their voids. It should be another good season for the team, especially with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren leading the way.

articles.title: Chargers’ Tony Jefferson drops defiant take amid brutal 0-6 situation
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers continue to sink further in the 2026 season. Now the Kansas City Chiefs dropped them to 0-6 following the 22-6 loss at Arrowhead Sta...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers continue to sink further in the 2026 season. Now the Kansas City Chiefs dropped them to 0-6 following the 22-6 loss at Arrowhead Stadium. But Tony Jefferson dropped a defiant take.

The safety doesn't believe his team is dead in the water yet.

"Until they say we're dead, we're alive. So we're just gonna keep fighting," Jefferson said to reporters. "Nobody's going to lay down or quit."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Chargers and coach Jim Harbaugh will love that kind of confidence from one of their veteran leaders. But the Chargers are teetering towards finishing with their worst mark since the 2000 season.

That Bolts team ended up going 1-15, and that was the last time LAC started 0-6. So this is the first worst start in the Harbaugh regime.

Many point to Harbaugh not meshing with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel as a big reason behind the slow start. Granted, Harbaugh has denied in the past that he wouldn't take away the play-calling duties from McDaniel. Harbaugh's postgame words, though, paint a different picture.

"We have to address everything guys and especially offensively. We're not scoring enough points," Harbaugh said to reporters afterward. "We're going to look at everything. The job I'm doing, it starts with me. The plan is we'll watch this and get with our offensive coaches. … [Offense] Needs to be addressed."

So that paints the picture that Harbaugh and McDaniel may need to pivot to another direction offensively. Meanwhile on defense, Jefferson tallied five tackles and finished third there. But LAC allowed 422 total yards.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson Breaks Silence on Ejection
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills entered the bye week with a 33-31 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday afternoon, but C.J. Gardner-Johnson got ejected. The post Buffal...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills entered the bye week with a 33-31 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday afternoon.

Before the first half ended, Bills starting safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected for spitting near a Raiders player. The play resulted in a 15-yard penalty and a chance for the Raiders to take one shot at the end zone.

The Bills will enter their bye week with a record of 5-1.

C.J. Gardner-Johnson Apologizes to Buffalo Bills

After the ejection, Gardner-Johnson did face the music as he spoke to the media after the game.

Gardner-Johnson apologized to the team and said it was something he can't do, as it hurts the team.

"We were just arguing and talking," Gardner-Johnson told reporters postgame . "It was nothing negative. He ain't do nothing to me. It was just in the heat of the game arguing and talking s**t. That gesture isn't warranted."

Gardner-Johnson said he does expect to be fined for it, and knows he has to be better going forward.

"I got to be a better player, I got to be a better vet, I hurt my team," Gardner-Johnson said. I just go to control my emotions."

Although Gardner-Johnson knows he has to be better, whether or not he gets a chance to prove that is unclear. There are calls for the Bills to cut him after the ejection, as he's also struggled this season, which could lead to Damar Hamlin or Jalen Kilgore taking over his role.

Joe Brady Sends Message to Gardner-Johnson

Before Gardner-Johnson spoke to the media in the locker room, Joe Brady made his feelings clear about the ejection.

Brady said it's something the Bills will address and is something they can't allow.

"I haven't seen the clip yet. I was talking to the ref, they took it to New York and it was clear as day. I'm sure I'm going to see it shortly after here. At the end of the day, if it shows up, that can't happen; that's the discipline I'm talking about. It's uncalled for, it can't happen, and it's going to be addressed," Brady said .

Whether or not the Bills will move on from Gardner-Johnson is to be seen. But the team can use the bye week as a chance to bring in some safeties and perhaps take his job.

articles.title: Lukas Van Ness' roughing the passer penalty baffles Packers fans
articles.summary: Social media sounds off on the roughing the passer penalty called against Lukas Van Ness late in the Packers' game vs. the Dallas Cowboys.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged after the 23-13 win over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 6 his team has to clean up the penalties.

Before a national audience on "Sunday Night Football," the Packers had 11 penalties in the game, including multiple dead-ball infractions, for a total of 96 yards.

Four penalties actually came on one drive for the defense in the fourth quarter, with one taking away an interception.

But that roughing the passer penalty called against Packers edge rusher Lukas Van Ness in the fourth quarter had many on social media baffled with the referees.

The Packers led 23-7 at the time and Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott looked for wide receiver Jonathan Mingo. Carrington Valentine stepped in front of Mingo and picked it off.

However, that interception was negated when Van Ness was called for a late hit on Prescott.

Replays showed Van Ness pushed Prescott with two hands after he released the ball, though it wasn't high and it certainly didn't appear that it was done with any kind of force, even if it knocked the Cowboys QB off his feet.

The Cowboys continued the drive but it ended on downs and the Packers kept their two-score lead.

The penalties were part of a chippy game between the Packers and Cowboys, who were also called for 11 penalties totaling 108 yards.

articles.title: Messi Heads to Spain for Asturias Award, Eyes Miami Return
articles.summary: Lionel Messi will fly to Spain on October 22 to receive the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, becoming the first soccer player ever to win the honor. In...
articles.body:
Lionel Messi will fly to Spain on October 22 to receive the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, becoming the first soccer player ever to win the honor. Inter Miami expects him back in time for the club's MLS clash with the New York Red Bulls two days later.

The award, announced back in June, recognizes standout figures across sports, culture, science and international cooperation. The selection committee cited not just Messi's trophy haul but his influence on the global growth of the game.

Coach González said the club fully supports Messi's trip to Oviedo, calling the tribute meaningful for the player and his family. Despite the short window, Miami is confident its captain will be ready for the October 24 match in Harrison, New Jersey.

Inter Miami has already clinched a playoff berth, but the matchup still matters. The club is chasing Nashville for a better position in the Eastern Conference and wants to carry momentum into the postseason.

Messi arrives off another decisive outing. Germán Berterame opened the scoring in the 45th minute off a Messi-involved play against Atlanta United, then Messi took over in the second half. In the 56th minute, he collected the ball on the right, combined with Berterame, cut past the defense and finished low. Four minutes later, Luis Suárez sprung the counterattack and set him up again.

Atlanta pulled one back through a Fafa Picault penalty, but couldn't complete the comeback. González praised Messi's ability to keep deciding games at 39, saying he's never seen the forward play with more joy.

The two goals push Messi's season total to 25, extending his lead in the MLS Golden Boot race, with 15 assists to go with it. He's now at 936 career goals, with 1,000 standing as one of his last major individual targets.

The win over Atlanta was Inter Miami's third straight. With a playoff spot locked up, the focus now shifts to finishing strong, starting with the Red Bulls on October 24 — assuming Messi's trip to Spain goes as planned.

articles.title: How Notre Dame’s opponents fared in WEEK 7 of the CFB season
articles.summary: We’re keeping track of Notre Dame’s opponents and how they do each and every week — because it might be fun.
articles.body:
Notre Dame's 2026 college football schedule has been called many thing over the last eight months, but "tough" or anywhere near the word "hard" was certainly not among them. Still, some have mentioned that this Irish schedule could look a lot trickier as the season progresses. While they may eventually be true, it may not matter all that much (except for message boards and social media).

Notre Dame took a minute or two to get going against the Wisconsin Badgers in the season opener, but eventually the Irish whooped them 42-13. Notre Dame welcomed the Rice Owls to South Bend for the home opener, and sent them back to Texas with a 52-0 loss. Although the Irish were big favorites against Michigan State, they got their best shot — and still beat the Spartans 27-10. The Irish were once again massive favorites over a Big 10 team, and they more than covered against Purdue with a 49-10 win that was never that close. Notre Dame was better than a three touchdown favorite against North Carolina, but ran into a bit of a clunker (and rain) and beat the Tar Heels 37-26. After two weeks on the road, Notre Dame returned to South Bend and the homecooking did them well as the Irish destroyed the Stanford Cardinal 58-7. Disaster hit the Irish against BYU in a 28-24 loss, and no matter what part of the game you want to complain about (because there was quite a bit) the simplest thing to say is that Notre Dame flat out got outplayed by the Cougars. Notre Dame will now be able to chomp down some cheeseburgers during their bye week.

Notre Dame is still likely to be favored in every game this season, and they are still a popular pick to win the national championship. Their strength of schedule probably isn't going to matter much, but let's keep track of it anyway.
